core.title: Connect every rendering app component to the design system
core.given: A repository that has a design root (its shared design-system tree), and an app component file of the markup kind outside that design root which renders markup
core.when: any such component is assessed (new, edited, or untouched)
core.then: It MUST import at least one design-system element (token, primitive, component, or template) from the design root, so no UI surface is disconnected from the shared system.
prefer: Compose UI from the existing design-system template, component, or primitive that owns the required role.
During GREEN: reuse the nearest existing design-system surface; add only the connection the current rendered behavior requires.
During GREEN: if no suitable surface exists, introduce the smallest design-system component that expresses the current need.
avoid: A meaningless design import merely to satisfy connectivity.
A generic component library for hypothetical callers.
Redesigning the screen or migrating unrelated markup.
unless: No design root in the repo (not judged).
Test files and vendored/build trees (never scanned).
Non-rendering modules: boundary (routes, handlers, endpoints) and data modules (not judged).
core.why: A screen built without the system is where the next one-off style lands. Requiring one design import makes the connection explicit and reviewable.
evidence: The stack's design-system connectivity check reports no rendering component outside the design root lacking a design-root import.
The current behavioral or rendering acceptance passes.
Reviewer confirms the rendered app component is genuinely composed from the design system (the import is used for rendering, not decorative).
verification: Flag every markup-kind component file outside the design root that renders markup and imports nothing from the design root; all qualifying files are judged, not only changed ones.

Self-scoping: a repository with no design root is not judged (there is no system to connect to yet). Design-root existence is evaluated on the repository tree, separately from candidate-file matching.
A rendering component is recognized by the stack's markup-rendering construct (profile: idiom.rendering_component), examined with string literals and comments masked.

An import counts as a design-system import when it resolves under the design root (profile: roots.design_system); the element's kind (token, primitive, component, template) is identified by the design root's layer directories (profile: layout.design_layers).

Never scan test files or vendored/build trees, and do not judge non-rendering modules such as boundary handlers and data modules. The exact exclusion list is the stack's single never-scanned list, owned by the checker (profile: roots.excluded); the rule does not restate it.

fires: A markup-kind app component outside the design root renders markup and imports nothing from the design root, while the repository has a design root

doesNotFire: The repository has no design root (no shared design system)

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the repository's shared design system (design root) lives. Three uses: (a) repository-level precondition — absence self-scopes the rule for the whole repository; (b) candidate-file scope — files under it are not judged; (c) import resolution — an import resolving under it is a design-system import. In the Bun realization any directory with one of these names qualifies (globs **/design/, **/design_system/, **/design-system/).

The internal layer-directory layout of the design root: which first-level directories beneath it name which design-system layer (token, primitive, component, template), so the kind of an imported design-system element can be identified. Other stacks supply their corresponding design-system layer layout here.
profileRequirements.bunValue: The first directory beneath it names the layer: `tokens` or `foundations`, `primitives`, `components`, `templates`.

profileRequirements.meaning: The file suffixes that mark a source file as a markup-kind (rendering) component; these are the candidate files.
The stack's test-file name patterns, never scanned (the ATDD-Bun realization uses one pattern family for all test kinds).
The stack's single never-scanned list of vendored/build trees; the checker that owns the exact classification is authoritative.
How the stack recognizes that a component source file renders markup: which construct counts as rendering, and what is masked before looking for it.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a component source file whose code (literals and comments masked) contains a closing tag or a self-closing element

proposedKeys.meaning: Globs or directories under which the repository's shared design system (design root) lives; used for the repository-level existence precondition, for excluding design-system files themselves from candidacy, and for resolving which imports are design-system imports.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The roots group has config, source, test, e2e, plan, scan and excluded only; no existing key locates the shared design-system tree.

proposedKeys.meaning: The internal layer-directory layout of the design root: which first-level directories beneath it name which design-system layer (token, primitive, component, template), so the kind of an imported design-system element can be identified; each stack supplies its own design-system layer layout.
proposedKeys.bunValue: The first directory beneath it names the layer: `tokens` or `foundations`, `primitives`, `components`, `templates`.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The layout group covers wagon, feature, commons, code-tree, plan-item, test and e2e placement only; no existing key describes the layer directories inside the design root.

proposedKeys.meaning: How the stack recognizes that a component source file renders markup: the construct that counts as rendering, and what is masked (literals, comments) before looking for it.
proposedKeys.bunValue: a component source file whose code (literals and comments masked) contains a closing tag or a self-closing element
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.markup_kinds names markup artifact kinds (static pages, templates) in which declarative request/gate constructs appear; it does not define the source-level recognition of a component that renders markup.

bunOnly.reason: The detection mechanics are per-stack (profile: idiom.rendering_component plus the stack's import resolution) and the detector id bun_design_system_detector names this rule's Bun realization.

neutralityNotes: The core keeps the ATDD phase term 'During GREEN' and the design-system taxonomy (token, primitive, component, template), both stack-neutral. Three profile keys had to be proposed because the closed vocabulary has no home for them: roots.design_system (design-root location), layout.design_layers (the design root's internal layer-directory mapping, moved out of bunOnly per audit because it is layout data other stacks must supply), and idiom.rendering_component (what counts as rendering markup). The concrete vendored/build globs and the authority of the detector's own exclusion list stay in core:verification, per the Bun text's declared-addition note; roots.excluded remains the single stack-wide list. Only the detector id bun_design_system_detector remains bunOnly (in evidence[0] and activation.facts[4]): it names this rule's Bun realization and has no stack-neutral equivalent. All bunValue strings are quoted verbatim from bun.json (the design-root directory names and layer mapping from verifier_detail[0], the markup suffixes from given/verifier_detail[3], the test patterns from unless[1], the vendored/build globs from the declared addition in additions[0]).
